title: Hurricane Simon Hit 155 mph. NASA Watched It Shake the Edge of Space

scenes.text: 155 miles an hour. This hurricane shook the edge of space.
Hurricane Simon, October 2026. Category 4, sitting 30 miles off Mexico.
scenes.keywords: hurricane waves crashing coast palm trees

scenes.text: Hurricane winds 25 miles from the eye. Up to 30 inches of rain.
Then a NASA satellite looked down at night and saw rings. Ripples, 50 miles above the storm.
Its updrafts punch the air so hard that waves roll upward, like a stone dropped in a pond.
scenes.keywords: ripples water stone drop slow motion

scenes.text: A storm making waves at the edge of space. 155 miles an hour.

description:
Hurricane Simon reached Category 4 in October 2026 with sustained winds of 155 miles an hour while its eye sat about 30 miles off Mexico's Pacific coast between Manzanillo and Puerto Vallarta.
A NASA satellite's night-time sensor captured concentric gravity waves rippling through the faint airglow high above the storm, created by its violent updrafts. Hurricane-force winds stretched 25 miles from the centre and forecasters warned of up to 30 inches of rain.
Have you ever been through a hurricane? Comment below.
first_comment: The ripples show up in a glow layer about 50 miles up, far above where any plane flies. Which is scarier: the wind, the rain, or the sea?
